item.title: Remote from abroad on holiday: cross-border taxes
item.description: Working remotely during a holiday in a third country: how taxation works, what LAMal covers and whether the employer needs to be informed. Practical guide for border workers Ticino-Italy.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Withholding tax remains in Switzerland, not "in both countries" - Italy grants a tax credit to avoid double taxation - Communicating international telework to the employer is mandatory - LAMal remains covered throughout the foreign stay
## Key facts - **What**: Remote telework for a Swiss employer during vacation in a third country - When: During smart working days (not official holidays) - Where: Any foreign country (not CH, not bordering Italy) - Who: Cross-border commuters with Permit G/B residing in Italy, employed by a Swiss company - Legislation: New Cross-Border Agreement (effective 1 January 2024); Italy-Switzerland Double Taxation Convention (9 December 1976) - Tax: Single withholding in Switzerland; Italian tax credit - Coverage: LAMal continues without interruption
A cross-border commuter working remotely during a vacation in a third country moves between three tax systems: Switzerland (where the employer is based), Italy (tax residence of the commuter), and the temporary stay country. The New Cross-Border Agreement, effective 1 January 2024, has clarified how to avoid double taxation, but practical doubts remain regarding taxation and obligations towards the employer.
### The withholding tax regime remains unchanged
Swiss withholding tax applies regardless of where the cross-border commuter is physically located. The employer continues to withhold tax according to the applicable cantonal rate, without considering the temporary stay country. This is a crucial point: taxation occurs ONCE, in Switzerland, never in duplicate.
Italy, thanks to the Convention between the two countries signed on 9 December 1976 and the criteria of the New Agreement, DOES NOT apply a second taxation on the employment income already subject to Swiss withholding tax. The cross-border commuter declares the income in the CE section of the Italian model 730, indicating the gross amount and the taxes paid in Switzerland. The Italian tax authority automatically issues a proportional tax credit, reducing or eliminating additional Italian taxation.
### Communication to the employer: not optional
Informing the employer of the situation (dates of stay, days of international telework, destination country) is not just a courtesy; it is an obligation. Two reasons: first, the employer has the right to know where their employees work for reasons of civil liability, operational continuity, and GDPR compliance (some countries have different data protection rules). Second, written documentation of the communication protects the cross-border commuter in case of subsequent tax audits.
An email to the HR manager with the exact dates, the destination country, and the request for confirmation of the availability of international smart working creates a record that justifies the tax situation before the Italian Revenue Agency or the Swiss cantonal authority. ### LAMal: continuous cover also from abroad
The most frequently asked question is: Does LAMal (Swiss health insurance) cover the border worker if they work remotely from a foreign country? The answer is yes, no exceptions. The Swiss LAMal covers the border crossing (G permit) throughout the world, including during temporary stay in third countries, as long as it remains enrolled in the Swiss insurance. There is no interruption of coverage, lapse of the policy, or request for information from the insurer before departure.
However, it is prudent to check three aspects of your coverage:
- **LPP (mandatory employer pension)**: Some integrated plans include explicit clauses on coverage during international work. Check your collective bargaining agreement or company LPP membership document for geo exclusions. - LAINF (Swiss Accident Insurance): Coverage for accidents while teleworking abroad is generally included, but some employers or insurance intermediaries may apply restrictions on non-EU countries. Ask your employer or intermediary before you leave. - Health conventions of the country of destination: If the country of destination has agreements with Switzerland (e.g. EU), costs are generally covered. Non-EU countries may incur out-of-pocket costs; check if your supplementary/private insurance covers these differences.
### Italian tax declaration: the framework
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Pre-departure checklist
1. Written notification to the employer (MANDATORY) Send an email to the HR manager or direct supervisor containing: - Exact departure and return dates - Days you will continue to work remotely - Destination country (relevant information for GDPR and civil liability issues) - Contact availability (time zone, emergency number) Request a written confirmation of the company's availability for international teleworking.
**2. Insurance coverage verification** Check your LAMal policy for geographical exclusions (rare, but some private integrated policies may have limitations). Read the documentation of the company's LPP (mandatory pension) for coverage during foreign work. Verify with the employer's insurance broker if LAINF (accidents) covers smart working from a third country or has exclusions for specific areas.
3. Tax documentation Gather and organize: - Email communication to the employer (situation attestation) - Work communication extracts (emails, chat messages) attesting to teleworking days vs. vacation - Certification of residence in Italy (useful if subsequent checks) - Copy of the current LAMal policy
### Deadlines and declarative procedure
The ordinary tax deadlines remain unchanged:
- December 31, 2026: The Swiss employer issues the Certificazione Unica (CU) with the work income and withholding taxes deducted during the year. - May 15–31, 2027: Deadline for submitting the Italian income tax return (model 730 or model Redditi). If submitted electronically via a CAF intermediary, the deadline may extend to June 30.
In the model 730, enter the declared income in the "Employment Income" section and complete the CE section indicating the taxes paid in Switzerland. The Italian Revenue Agency processes the tax credit automatically; the bank communicates the refund amount (or deduction) within the ordinary deadlines.
### Tools and support: tax calculator Use the [tax calculator](nav:calculator) of Frontaliere Ticino to estimate your annual net income considering: - Cantonale withholding tax rate (Ticino: about 8–10%, variable by company and family situation) - Italian IRPEF brackets (23% up to €28,000; 35% from €28,001 to €50,000; 43% over €50,000) - Italian tax credit automatically applied if declared correctly
For questions about AVS/AI (mandatory Swiss pension) and LPP (employer pension), consult the [pension comparator](nav:pension). If you need personalized advice on specific tax implications of your case, contact the Italian Revenue Agency or the cantonal tax administration (AFC/ESTV) in Switzerland.

item.title: Remote border crossing: taxes and fees from the holiday
item.description: Do you work remotely from abroad? Taxation remains in Switzerland. Tax at source, AVS, LAMal: what changes with the new 2024 border agreement.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Withholding tax remains in Switzerland, does not change if you work from abroad - AVS/LPP/LAMal remain active for cross-border workers with a Swiss employer - New agreement 2024: threshold €7,500 (old) or €10,000 (new cross-border workers) - Notify employer: contractual and insurance obligation
## Key facts - **What**: Remote work from a third country for cross-border workers with a Swiss employer - When: Rules apply from 1 January 2024 (new agreement) - Where: Any country outside Switzerland and Italy - Who: Cross-border workers G (weekly cross-border workers) - Taxation: Swiss withholding tax 5.3% (AVS/AI/IPG employee) - Threshold: €7,500 (cross-border workers pre-17/7/2023) or €10,000 (new) - Insurance: LAMal mandatory, CHF 300–2500 annual deductible
A cross-border worker who spends three weeks in Portugal continuing to work remotely for their Ticino-based employer faces a recurring question: how is the income taxed? Which country has the right to tax it?
The answer is clear: the withholding tax remains in Switzerland. The new physical place of work (the third country) does not have the right to tax the employment income because the relationship remains subordinate to a Swiss employer. The legal basis is the Convention between Italy and Switzerland of 9 December 1976 on double taxation and the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement which came into force on 1 January 2024 (Law 83 of 13 June 2023 for Italy). These instruments clarify that taxation follows the location of the employer, not the location of the employee at the time of work.
### Taxation: the income remains Swiss
Concretely, a cross-border worker earning CHF 60,000 annually continues to pay AVS/AI/IPG at 5.3% (Swiss employee contribution), amounting to CHF 3,180 annually, regardless of where they are during the contract. Additional contributions (AD/AC at 1.1% up to CHF 148,200 of income, LAINF 0.7–1.5% for accidents, LPP 7–18% for pension according to age bracket) remain unchanged.
Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit in the CE section of the 730 declaration, where the cross-border worker declares the Swiss income and recovers the tax withheld in Switzerland. The mechanism is automatic for cross-border workers who complete the declaration: the Tax Agency recognizes the payment made in Switzerland and deducts it from the Italian IRPEF.
### The new 2024 agreement and the thresholds
With the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement, cross-border workers already classified as such before 17 July 2023 benefit from a threshold of €7,500 on income, valid until 2033 in a transitional regime. Cross-border workers hired after that date have a threshold of €10,000. This partial exemption remains valid even in the case of remote work from abroad during holidays, and does not require special notification to Swiss or Italian authorities if the vacation falls within normal limits (up to 4–6 weeks). However, notifying the employer remains mandatory both contractually and insurancely. ### AVS, LPP and LAMal during remote work
While withholding tax follows the employer's location, pension and insurance rights require special attention. AVS (old-age and survivors' insurance) and AI (disability insurance) continue to accrue contribution rights, regardless of where the cross-border worker is during remote work.
The LPP (occupational pension scheme) continues regularly: if the employer has a collective plan (as in almost all Swiss companies), contributions follow the age bracket table of the cross-border worker. If the cross-border worker turns 25 during a work break, LPP enrollment kicks in and the employer starts contributing the purpose quota (7–18% of gross income).
LAMal (health insurance) is the most delicate point. Category G cross-border workers (weekly cross-border workers, representing almost all Ticino-Italy commuters) have the option to remain insured in Switzerland or switch to the Italian INPS system. If they stay in Switzerland, they maintain the annual deductible between CHF 300 and CHF 2500 for adults. During remote work, LAMal remains valid.
A practical issue: if the cross-border worker stays more than 90 days in a third country, they might lose their weekly cross-border status for that tax declaration, with consequences for deductibles and residence rights. For normal vacations (up to 4–6 weeks), there are no risks.
### Accident and liability coverage
LAINF (Law on Accident Insurance) covers work-related accidents, wherever the cross-border worker is. If a fall down the stairs during home office in Portugal results in an injury, Swiss LAINF responds regularly. The employer remains responsible for keeping LAINF coverage active, without the need for additional communications for remote work.
However, if the cross-border worker engages in activities in violation of the agreement with the employer (for example, working from a country where the contract explicitly prohibits it) and gets injured, civil liability may shift to the employee or be contested by the insurer. Therefore, notifying the employer in advance is both a legal protection and a practical convention. The [complete LAMal coverage for cross-border workers](nav:health) explores specific options.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Practical procedure: the 5 steps
If you are planning a remote vacation, following these steps can reduce the risks of misunderstandings or contractual violations.
1. Read the employment contract. Check if it contains clauses on working from abroad, limits on days/months of remote work abroad, or geographical exclusions. Many Swiss contracts allow up to 2–4 weeks without authorization; beyond that, HR approval is required.
2. Notify your employer at least 2–3 weeks in advance. Send a formal email to the HR manager indicating: the vacation period, the country of work, and your contact details during regular working hours. An example: "From August 12 to 26, I will be on vacation in Barcelona, but I will continue to work remotely. I will remain reachable via email."
3. Verify VPN coverage and data confidentiality. Your employer may require an encrypted connection to protect company data. Set up a company or personal VPN before departure.
4. Do not change your address of residence. If the cross-border commuter intends to actually change their residence from Ticino to a third country, the cross-border commuter status changes radically and may lose AVS and VAT rights. For vacations, remain registered at your Ticino address.
5. Optional communication to the Tax Agency. If the remote vacation exceeds 4 weeks, consider notifying via PEC to your CAF or the Tax Agency that you will continue to work remotely. This is not mandatory for short vacations, but it avoids surprises in case of subsequent verification.
### Calculate your net income and check refunds
To evaluate the precise tax impact of your situation, use the [cross-border tax calculator](nav:calculator). Enter your gross income, start date as a cross-border commuter, and you will get an estimate of the net income after AVS/LPP/LAMal.
With the new 2024 agreement and the allowances €7.500–€10.000, many cross-border commuters discover they are entitled to refunds of taxes paid in excess in previous years. Consult the guide [how to request cross-border refunds](nav:ristorni) to see if it applies to your situation.
The tax implications of remote work are complex, but the basic principle remains simple: the employer decides the country of taxation. We keep your rights transparent and updated to the 2024 regulations.

item.title: Tax reform: Personal income tax deductions without cohabitation
item.description: The new tax reform eliminates the obligation to live together for personal income tax deductions on dependent family members, with important implications for border workers.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The tax reform reorganizes the chapter on dependents. - Co-habitation is no longer mandatory for IRPEF deductions. - Reimbursement of the RSA fee for a non-cohabiting parent is exempt from IRPEF.
## Key facts - **What**: Tax reform on dependents. - When: From 20 December 2025. - Where: Italy. - Who: Italian Revenue Agency. - Amount: Not specified.
The tax reform has recently made significant changes to the chapter on dependents, after two years of corrections that had narrowed and then reopened the scope. The latest intervention, contained in the Omnibus amendment, has canceled the restriction that, from 2025, had excluded brothers, parents-in-law, sons-in-law, and daughters-in-law from the fiscal notion of a dependent, along with parents who do not live with the taxpayer. For deductions for children and dependents in the tax return, nothing changes, while the most immediate consequence is found in the area of corporate welfare, where the Italian Revenue Agency has just recognized the exemption for a reimbursement paid in favor of a non-cohabiting dependent. The correction applies retroactively and affects amounts that many companies have already taxed.
### Changes to the TUIR The article 1 of the Legislative Decree 7 August 2026, n. 148 rewrites paragraph 4-ter of article 12 of the TUIR. The changes apply from the tax period in progress as of 20 December 2025, therefore already for the tax year 2025. With the ruling n. 163 of 14 August 2026, the Italian Revenue Agency excludes from IRPEF the reimbursement of the RSA fee for a non-cohabiting parent. Co-habitation or non-judicial maintenance payments are relevant where the rule requires the dependent to be fiscally dependent. The deduction for family charges of ascendants continues to require co-habitation.
### Concrete examples Suppose a taxpayer from Lugano has an elderly parent who resides in an RSA in Bellinzona. Until 2025, the reimbursement of the RSA fee was not exempt from IRPEF if the parent did not live with the taxpayer. With the new reform, this reimbursement will be exempt from IRPEF, allowing the taxpayer to save about 1,000 euros per year, considering a monthly fee of 1,500 euros.
### Operational checklist 1. Check co-habitation: Ensure that the non-cohabiting dependent is fiscally dependent. 2. Documentation: Keep documents that certify the expense incurred for the non-cohabiting dependent. 3. Tax return: Correctly enter the deductions in the tax return. 4. Consultation with an expert: In case of doubts, consult an accountant or tax advisor.
### Comparisons between practical scenarios Scenario 1: A taxpayer from Mendrisio has a disabled brother who does not live with him. Until 2025, the brother was not considered a dependent for IRPEF deductions. With the new reform, the taxpayer will be able to benefit from the deductions, saving about 500 euros per year.
Scenario 2: A taxpayer from Locarno has an elderly mother-in-law who resides in an RSA in Chiasso. Until 2025, the reimbursement of the RSA fee was not exempt from IRPEF if the mother-in-law did not live with the taxpayer. With the new reform, this reimbursement will be exempt from IRPEF, allowing the taxpayer to save about 800 euros per year, considering a monthly fee of 1,200 euros.
### Key dates and regulations - Legislative Decree 7 August 2026, n. 148: Rewrites paragraph 4-ter of article 12 of the TUIR. - 20 December 2025: Date of entry into force of the changes. - Ruling n. 163 of 14 August 2026: Excludes from IRPEF the reimbursement of the RSA fee for a non-cohabiting parent.
### Conclusion The tax reform introduces significant changes for dependents, eliminating the obligation of co-habitation for IRPEF deductions and recognizing the exemption for the reimbursement of the RSA fee for non-cohabiting parents. These changes will have a positive impact on many taxpayers, allowing them to save hundreds of euros per year. It is essential to be informed and prepared to fully benefit from these new provisions.
⚠️ Attention: The information provided is for informational purposes only and does not constitute tax advice. For personalized advice, consult a professional. ## Tax reform: Personal income tax deductions without cohabitation The expenses incurred for parents, brothers, sisters, in-laws, sons-in-law and daughter-in-law are again recognised for the purposes of the tax benefits linked to Article 12 of the TUIR even when the family member lives elsewhere. Article 1 of Legislative Decree no. 148 of 7 August 2026, published in ordinary supplement no. 30 to Official Gazette no. 185 of 11 August 2026, abolishes from the first period of paragraph 4-ter the condition of cohabitation with the taxpayer or the receipt of alimony checks not resulting from measures of the judicial authority. That condition is reintroduced only in the second period, which defines the dependent family member, and moreover limited to the persons listed in Article 433 of the Civil Code other than the spouse and children. The same amendment is replicated in Article 12, paragraph 7 of the new Consolidated Law on Income Tax, Legislative Decree no. 117 of 19 June 2026, which will apply from 2027. # ## Concrete examples Imagine a taxpayer living in Lugano who incurs medical expenses for his elderly father, who lives in Bellinzona. Until 2024, the father had to live with the taxpayer or receive alimony to be considered fiscally dependent. With the new legislation, the father can be considered a dependent even if he does not live with the taxpayer, as long as he falls within the categories provided for in Article 433 of the Civil Code. # ## Importantly, the new regulations will take effect from 2027, and taxpayers need to adjust to the new guidelines to avoid tax penalties. item.title: Bally Caslano: 79 layoffs in one move
item.description: The multinational announces the cutting of 25 administrative staff and 54 operational staff. Protests of the Council of State on the free market. What does the cross-border commuters need to know?
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Bally Caslano announces collective dismissal of 79 employees (25 administrative, 54 operational) - The reduction is part of a structural process already underway ("umpteenth" dismissal) - Direct notification to workers and cantonal offices in Ticino - The Council of State confirms the applicability of the competitive framework
## Key facts - **What**: Collective redundancy at Bally Caslano - When: Recent announcement (specific date not communicated by source) - Where: Caslano, Canton of Ticino - Who: Bally (operating company from Zug) - Impacted: 79 total employees - Composition: 25 administrative staff, 54 operational employees - Notification: Direct communication to workers and cantonal offices
The company Bally, led by Zug, has announced a massive new collective redundancy at the Caslano plant. According to the notice communicated to Ticino employees and cantonal offices, this tranche involves 79 people: 25 administrative sector employees and 54 operational employees of the plant.
The use of the word "umpteenth" in the press release reveals that this reduction is part of a process of structural contraction already underway. The company does not provide details on specific economic reasons or implementation history. This silence is typical in business communications during critical situations: the formal announcement usually precedes the analytical communications.
### The institutional role and the framework ## What collective redundancy means for the frontier worker
Under Swiss law, collective redundancy is a procedure that affects at least 10 employees over a period of 30 days. Bally Caslano, with 79 people involved, far exceeds this threshold. Communication to workers must be in writing and must include the economic, technical or organisational reasons behind the decision.
For an Italian border worker employed at Bally Caslano, the dismissal activates rights protected by both Swiss (workplace) and Italian (place of residence) legislation. The Swiss employer cannot exempt itself from its obligations towards the border worker: the notice remains binding according to the contract, and severance pay follows the applicable Swiss legislation. The border worker does not lose protection for the mere fact of residing in Italy.
### Concrete protections: CAD and acquired contributions
A key protection is registration with the **CAD** (Unemployment Insurance Fund), which is mandatory for all employees in Switzerland, including frontier workers. When the dismissal comes into effect and the border worker remains unemployed, he/she is entitled to unemployment benefits of the CAD based on contributions paid during employment. The duration of the allowance depends on the length of service and the age of the worker.

## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Immediate actions for the dismissed cross-border worker
If you are a cross-border worker affected by the Bally Caslano dismissal, the next steps are crucial and require promptness. Swiss and Italian authorities have specific deadlines for activating your rights.
### Step 1: Verify the formal terms of the dismissal
Request a complete and certified copy of the dismissal notice in writing. Ensure it clearly indicates: - The exact termination date - The notice period applied (days or months, and from which date it starts) - The reason (collective dismissal for economic/organizational reasons, in your case) - The address to receive the final documentation
Keep all official company messages, pay slips from the last 6 months, and the original employment contract.
### Step 2: Check the contribution balance with CAD
Access your individual account with the CAD of the Canton Ticino (online or at the office) and verify the total contributions paid since your start date at Bally. This amount directly determines your right and the duration of unemployment benefits. If the recorded contributions do not match your pay slips, report the discrepancy immediately: you have the right to correction.
### Step 3: Register with the Ticino Employment Office
Before the notice period expires (or immediately afterward), register with the Employment Office of the Canton Ticino. This formal step officially activates your right to CAD benefits and documents your active job search. If you permanently reside in Italy, provide your permanent address and cell phone number: you will remain contactable for job offers in Ticino and can maintain them from your home.
### Step 4: Recalculate the final pay slip
The employer is required to issue a final pay slip (on the last day of work) that includes: - Salary up to the indicated termination date - Any compensation for unused vacation (usually paid as additional salary) - Standard tax deductions (Swiss withholding tax for cross-border workers, to be declared to the Italian Revenue Agency) - Final contributions AVS/AI/IPG (5.3% employee), AD/AC (1.1%), LAINF (0.7-1.5%), LPP according to age bracket
Verify that the gross total and net total correspond to ordinary rules: no expected deductions should be missing, nor should there be any illegitimate reductions.
### Step 5: Declare unemployment in Italy
Simultaneously with the CAD registration in Switzerland, notify the Italian Employment Center of your province of residence about your unemployment situation. This activates your right to Italian unemployment benefits (NASpI) for subsequent periods, if the requirements (last 4 years of INPS contributions, etc.) are met. The procedure is independent of the Swiss CAD, but the two protections can be coordinated.
### Step 6: Post-dismissal financial planning
Use [our salary calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate the net amount you will receive in the final pay slip, considering the mandatory Swiss contributions and the withholding tax for cross-border workers. This allows you to plan your cash flow during the transition to new employment.
Time is critical: unemployment rights must be activated within specific deadlines (usually within 8 days of the termination date), and each lost day reduces recovery chances. Contact immediately: - **CAD Canton Ticino**: For the contribution balance and starting the unemployment procedure - Ticino Employment Office: For registration and active job search - Italian Employment Center: For synchronizing Italian unemployment rights
In this transition phase, precise planning is essential. Do not delay.

item.title: Living in Orino and working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Moving to Orino as a border worker: G Permit, tax at source and administrative procedure for work in Ticino.

## In brief - Cross-border workers with Permit G: withholding tax ONLY in Switzerland, no double taxation - New Cross-border Agreement: effective from 1 January 2024, allowances up to EUR 10,000 annually - Border crossings to Ticino: Brogeda, Gaggiolo, Ponte Tresa accessible from municipalities such as Orino - Complete procedure: Italian and Swiss documentation, mandatory tax registration and LAMal
## Key facts - **What**: Transfer of cross-border workers from Orino to work in Ticino with Permit G - When: Effective from 1 January 2024 (New Cross-border Agreement, signed 23 December 2020) - Where: Italian border municipalities (Orino, province of Varese) towards Ticino poles (Lugano, Bellinzona, Mendrisio, Locarno) - Who: EU/EEA cross-border workers within 55 km of the border with a Swiss employer contract - Tax: Withholding tax ONLY in Switzerland, tax credit in Italy (CE section of the 730) - Allowance: EUR 7,500 (cross-border workers pre-17 July 2023), EUR 10,000 (new cross-border workers) - Contributions: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% employee, AD/AC 1.1%, LAINF 0.7–1.5%, LPP 7–18% by age group
Choosing to live in Orino while working in Ticino is an increasingly adopted solution by cross-border workers to combine a higher quality of life with lower housing costs compared to the Swiss territory. Permit G allows Italian citizens to work in Switzerland while maintaining their residence in Italy, without fiscal complications: the withholding tax is exclusively in Switzerland, while Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit attached to the income tax return in the 730 model (CE section). This regime, further stabilized by the New Cross-border Agreement effective from 1 January 2024, creates a predictable regulatory framework for those wishing to move to municipalities in the province of Varese such as Orino.
### Location and accessibility for cross-border commuting
Orino, located in the province of Varese, offers a strategic position to reach the main employment poles of Ticino — Lugano, Bellinzona, Mendrisio, Locarno — without incurring the housing costs of the Swiss territory. The proximity to the Brogeda and Gaggiolo border crossings, as well as to Ponte Tresa, reduces daily travel times, a crucial element for those facing cross-border commuting on a daily basis. Living costs, especially housing, are significantly lower compared to Ticino, allowing cross-border workers to preserve a larger share of their net income after taxes. Additionally, access to Italian services — schools, healthcare through INPS, local community — allows the cross-border worker to maintain a family and social life context in Italian territory.
### Taxation: withholding tax and allowances of the new agreement
The tax regime of cross-border workers with Permit G is based on two pillars: the withholding tax exclusively withheld by the Swiss employer, and the Italian tax credit. The withholding is operated according to the federal and cantonal rates applicable to the canton of work. In the Italian 730 model, the cross-border worker declares the income received in Switzerland and benefits from the CE section for the tax credit, which compensates for the taxation already paid north of the Alps and ensures the principle of non-double taxation sanctioned by the Italy-Switzerland Convention of 9 December 1976. The New Cross-border Agreement has introduced differentiated allowances: those who were already cross-border workers before 17 July 2023 benefit from an annual allowance of EUR 7,500 (transitional regime 2024–2033), while new cross-border workers are entitled to an allowance of EUR 10,000. This mechanism further reduces Italian taxation on cross-border income. ### Advantages of choosing to live in Orino as a cross-border commuter
Moving to Orino offers concrete advantages for quality of life and economic management. Firstly, the cost of living — rent, food, general services — is significantly lower than in Ticino, allowing cross-border commuters to save money or reinvest in other areas. Secondly, maintaining Italian residency provides direct access to Italian public services (registration with INPS, Italian schooling, healthcare through the National Health Service when necessary) and the ability to remain in a culturally relevant community. Thirdly, the Permesso G provides administrative stability: the permit is renewable and allows daily movements without the need for a visa. Finally, the tax benefits of the New Cross-Border Agreement (exemptions, tax credit, no double taxation) significantly reduce the tax burden compared to other work configurations.
### Disadvantages and challenges of cross-border commuting
However, this choice also involves operational challenges. Daily commuting to the border crossings introduces variability in travel times: times depend on seasonal and daily traffic, queues at border crossings during peak hours, and potential disruptions (strikes, adverse weather conditions, customs checks). Secondly, managing the administration of two countries — Italian taxes, registrations with Italian entities (INPS, Agenzia delle Entrate), Swiss health insurance, Swiss pension — requires competence and attention to deadlines for declarations and payments. Additionally, currency exchange (income in CHF, expenses in EUR) exposes the cross-border commuter to fluctuations in the exchange rate. Finally, the costs of mandatory health insurance (LAMal) and Swiss pension contributions (AVS, LPP) represent significant expenses, although recognized by the Italian system through the 1976 Convention.
### Pension and health insurance: practical organization
A critical aspect for relocation is the organization of pension and health coverage. Mandatory health insurance (LAMal) must be taken out with a recognized Swiss insurer; cross-border commuters with Permesso G have the option to choose between Swiss LAMal and Italian insurance, but usually opt for the Swiss one to avoid administrative duplication and maintain consistency with the Swiss employer. The adult deductibles for LAMal range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 depending on the insurer and canton. Swiss contributions are significant: AVS/AI/IPG (old-age, disability, loss of earnings insurance) amounts to 5.3% for the employee, unemployment insurance AD/AC at 1.1% (with a cap of CHF 148,200), and accident insurance LAINF between 0.7% and 1.5%. If enrolled in LPP (mandatory occupational pension), the additional contribution varies from 7% to 18% depending on the age group (from the 25th year onwards). Overall, these contributions represent 15–25% of gross salary. Italy recognizes contributions paid in Switzerland through the Bilateral Convention of December 9, 1976, allowing the cross-border commuter to accumulate contribution periods for calculating the Italian pension with INPS. To explore the available health insurance options, consult the resources [dedicated to LAMal and health coverage](nav:health) on our site.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Practical procedure: documents and deadlines
Moving to Orino as a cross-border worker requires a sequence of administrative steps involving both Italy and Switzerland. In Italy: you must request a residence certificate from the municipality of Orino, register the move with the Revenue Agency (change of residence declaration), and notify the INPS of your new address so that the contributions paid in Switzerland are recognized in the pension scheme. In Switzerland: you need to have a work contract with a Swiss employer (prerequisite for the G Permit), then apply for the G Permit at the immigration office (SEM) of the Ticino canton, register with the Cantonal Statistical Office (USTAT) for the registry, and register with the Federal Tax Administration (AFC/ESTV) for withholding tax. In parallel, you must subscribe to the LAMal with a Swiss insurer and notify your employer of the automatic enrollment in AVS and LPP. Those who choose the third pillar 3a for supplementary pension must subscribe to a policy with a Swiss bank or management company.
### Deadlines and critical timelines
The New Cross-Border Agreement, effective from January 1, 2024, introduces precise deadlines for declarations and exemptions. Those moving after this date must comply with the terms for the initial declaration within the Italian tax deadlines (usually by April 30 of the following year for the 730). It is advisable to complete the administrative procedures within the first 30–60 days from the actual change of residence to avoid administrative penalties or interruptions in insurance coverage (e.g., uncovered periods of LAMal). The Italian tax return in the 730 model must include the CE section for the tax credit, an essential element for receiving the refund of the tax excess. Those starting work in Switzerland for the first time must pay attention to the AVS and LPP enrollment deadlines, as the employer is legally obliged to make these enrollments within specific legal terms.
### Calculation and planning tools
To estimate the impact of withholding tax in Switzerland on your net income, use the [Frontaliere Ticino tax calculator](nav:calculator). The tool allows you to simulate different salary scenarios and view the comparison between the Swiss gross, withholding tax, Italian tax credit, and net income in CHF and EUR. Once you have obtained the G Permit and moved to Orino, you can consult the [complete guide to tax refunds](nav:ristorni) to understand how to correctly fill out the CE section of the 730 declaration and maximize the tax recovery due to the deductibility of the Swiss tax credit. These tools will allow you to plan your move with real data and accurate forecasts on your family budget.

item.title: Living in Cittiglio and working in Ticino: border guide
item.description: Cittiglio as a housing area for border workers: taxation, G permit, living costs and advantages of transferring from Varese to the Canton of Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New Cross-border Agreement effective from January 1, 2024, with benefits for both old and new cross-border workers - Withholding tax deducted only in Switzerland for those working in Canton Ticino - Cittiglio offers competitive housing costs while maintaining cross-border tax benefits - Transitional regime until 2033 for those who were already cross-border workers before July 2023
## Key facts - **What**: New bilateral agreement between Switzerland and Italy on the cross-border regime - When: Signed on December 23, 2020, effective from January 1, 2024 - Where: Canton Ticino and bordering Italian municipalities in the province of Varese - Who: Cross-border workers with permit G; Italian ratification: Law 83 of June 13, 2023 - Amount: Old cross-border workers exemption €7,500, new €10,000 (until 2033)
Cittiglio, a municipality in the province of Varese located near the Ticino border, represents an interesting housing choice for cross-border workers who work in Canton Ticino. From January 1, 2024, the entry into force of the New Cross-border Agreement signed on December 23, 2020, has introduced significant benefits for those who choose to work in Switzerland and reside in Italy. The withholding tax on employment income is deducted only in Switzerland, avoiding double taxation. For old cross-border workers (those who were already cross-border workers before July 17, 2023), an annual exemption of €7,500 is provided in the first year, with a transitional regime until 2033. New cross-border workers benefit from a €10,000 exemption.
### The cross-border tax regime after the New Agreement
The taxation for those residing in Cittiglio and working in Ticino follows the model of the Italy-Switzerland Convention to avoid double taxation, signed on December 9, 1976. Italy recognizes the right of the cross-border worker to opt for the flat-rate regime, thus avoiding the submission of a complete tax return in Italy. In Switzerland, the taxpayer is subject to federal and cantonal rates, as well as contributions to AVS/AI/IPG (5.3% borne by the employee) and accident insurance LAINF (0.7–1.5% depending on the sector). The regime is particularly advantageous for those with a moderate income and a family in Italy.
Those residing in Cittiglio also have the option to choose [Swiss health insurance (LAMal)](nav:health), instead of maintaining Italian coverage. This choice can represent a saving if the management of double coverage is costly. LAMal costs vary based on age, gender, and canton of insurance, with adult deductibles ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500. Regarding pensions, the cross-border worker, by paying AVS/AI in Switzerland, accumulates pension rights that, combined with Italian INPS contributions, form a combined amount at the time of retirement.
### What to consider before moving to Cittiglio
Before choosing Cittiglio as a place of residence, it is essential to verify the status of cross-border worker (permit G) with the Ticino cantonal authorities and the documentation related to the declaration to the Italian tax authorities. Permit G is dedicated to EU/EFTA citizens who work in Switzerland and reside outside national borders. Registration with the Registry of Persons (Italian registry office) and communication to the Swiss tax authorities of the transfer are mandatory steps. It is not permitted to pretend a fixed residence if the stay is occasional; the cantonal authority can verify the actual domicile through telecommunications, the energy bill, and registration with local public services. ### Economic advantages of residing in Italy
Living in Cittiglio offers concrete economic advantages compared to staying in Ticino. Firstly, the [cost of living for rent and services](nav:cost-of-living) in the province of Varese is significantly lower than in urban centers in Ticino such as Lugano or Bellinzona. Although specific amounts are not available, it is known that the province of Varese offers competitive real estate opportunities compared to the Ticino market. A commuter who resides in Cittiglio maintains full access to Swiss tax benefits (taxation in Switzerland, exemption/allowance) while benefiting from Italian housing costs, creating a positive economic differential. Additionally, the general cost of living in Cittiglio (food, services, energy rates) is lower than in the Canton of Ticino, offering further monthly savings.
### The move: before and after the New Agreement
Before the entry into force of the New Agreement (1 January 2024), the tax regime was less favorable. Old commuters today benefit from a transitional regime that guarantees stability until 2033, reducing regulatory uncertainty. New commuters (from 17 July 2023 onwards) immediately access the €10,000 allowance, without an adjustment period. This change makes the choice to move to Cittiglio more attractive for those starting their commuter journey. Those who were already commuters before July 2023 can choose to adhere to the transitional regime, maintaining acquired benefits, or opt for the new regime if more convenient. Law 83 of 13 June 2023 ratified the New Agreement in Italy, providing full regulatory certainty.
### Disadvantages and risks of commuting
Living in Cittiglio also involves critical aspects. Daily commuting from Cittiglio to the main work centers in Ticino (Lugano, Mendrisio, Bellinzona, Locarno) requires crossing borders (Brogeda, Chiasso, Gaggiolo). Transborder commuting can expose to delays due to customs controls, traffic, strikes of public transport in Switzerland or Italy, and critical weather conditions in winter. The commuter must plan safety margins in travel times and consider the cost of mobility: regional transport subscriptions, Swiss vignettes for the car, fuel, maintenance. Furthermore, they must manage tax compliance in two systems (Italy and Switzerland), with different deadlines and double documentation; while benefiting from single taxation in Switzerland, communication to the Italian tax office and the flat-rate declaration require attention and precision. ### Practical procedure: checklist before moving
First step: obtain the [G permit](nav:permits) from the cantonal authority of residence in Ticino. Second: register with the Cittiglio Registry Office, indicating Switzerland as the place of work. Third: inform the Swiss employer of the move, who must notify the cantonal administration of contributions (AFC/ESTV) for the adjustment of withholding tax. Fourth: register with the Italian Revenue Agency in the new place of residence and indicate the frontier worker income. Fifth: check with the employer if the additional voluntary payment for the Swiss third pillar (3a) is available, which offers federal tax deductions. Sixth: choose whether to keep the Italian health insurance (CMI) or opt for the Swiss LAMal, considering costs and coverage.
### Tax deadlines to remember
Each year, the frontier worker residing in Cittiglio must comply with the Swiss tax deadlines related to the pay slip (the withholding tax is calculated monthly by the employer) and the Italian deadlines for the [flat-rate declaration](nav:tax-return) (usually by June of the following year, with terms set by the Revenue Agency). If the frontier worker adheres to the transitional regime (old frontier workers), they must verify the annual maintenance of the requirements for the €7,500 exemption. For those subject to additional payments (e.g., third pillar 3a), the deposit deadlines with the financial intermediary are usually set for December 31 of the relevant tax year. It is not allowed to postpone the communication to the Italian tax authorities; delay can result in administrative penalties.
### Support tools and advice
To simulate the tax impact of choosing to move to Cittiglio, the frontier worker can use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) of Frontaliere Ticino, which calculates the Swiss withholding tax, AVS/LPP contributions, and estimates the net monthly income. It is advisable to consult an Italian accountant specializing in frontier worker regimes (for IRPEF aspects and declaration) and a Swiss advisor for planning additional contributions and the third pillar. Some cantons in Ticino offer dedicated offices for frontier workers at the municipal administrations. The Italian-Swiss Convention (9 December 1976) and the New Agreement (effective from 1 January 2024) are available at the Italian Revenue Agency and the Swiss Federal AFC. Downloading these documents and reading them with a local expert reduces the risk of procedural errors and tax omissions. Do not rely on informal recommendations from friends; each personal situation (marital status, dependents, possible secondary income) can have different implications.

item.title: Construction: new six-year agreement in Ticino
item.description: The construction agreement is signed: construction allowance of up to 9 francs by 2028 and travel time counted from the first minute.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Construction agreement valid for the next 6 years. - New site allowances: from 4 CHF to 6.5 CHF (1st January 2027) up to 9 CHF. - Travel time to the site recorded from the first minute, with a 30-minute exemption removed.
## Key facts - **What**: Renewal of national and cantonal construction contracts. - When: Agreement signed in early May 2026. - Where: Switzerland and Canton Ticino. - Who: OCST and construction employers. - Amount: Site allowance 6.5 CHF from 1st January 2027.
The path leading to the recent contract renewal in the construction sector saw phases of intense mobilization. It was on 17 May 2025 when, in Zurich and Lausanne, negotiations for the renewal of the national contract began, with over 10,000 workers involved in union demands. After months of tense meetings and days of strikes across the Swiss territory, starting in Bellinzona on 20 October of the same year, a draft agreement was approved in mid-December. Subsequently, local negotiations for the cantonal contract led, in early May 2026, to the signing of a balanced agreement valid for the next six years. As communicated in June 2026, this new contractual framework marks a fundamental step for industrial relations in the sector. The OCST union, a key player in the negotiations, highlighted the importance of this result, which aims to stabilize the construction sector, composed of approximately 80,000 workers nationwide. The main demands, focused on maintaining purchasing power and shorter working days, found a response in a compromise that the parties defined as solid. The unusually long duration of the contract, equal to six years, was conceived to favor the normalization of relations between the union and employers, at a time when the sector must face crucial challenges, such as generational turnover and the increasing difficulty in finding qualified labor. The underlying strategy aims to improve the attractiveness of the profession by investing more confidently in professional training, a point considered essential to ensure the future sustainability of the construction site in Switzerland and Canton Ticino. ### Practical implications and working conditions
The contractual changes introduced will have direct and measurable impacts on the daily lives of construction workers. One of the central points concerns the management of travel times: the time required to reach the construction sites will now be recorded from the first minute, eliminating the 30-minute exemption that previously burdened operations. At the same time, a new site allowance has been introduced. Currently set at 4 francs per day, this item will undergo a scheduled increase: from January 1, 2027, it will rise to 6.5 francs, and then reach 9 francs per day in 2028. These changes represent a tangible adjustment for those who work daily in the field. Another significant aspect concerns the protection of wages: minimum wages will be automatically adjusted for the cost of living, providing dynamic protection against inflation. Furthermore, starting in 2029, a simple and clear mechanism will be activated to guarantee the purchasing power of real wages, offering a long-term financial stability perspective. For the cross-border worker operating in Ticino, these contractual provisions fit into the broader framework of withholding tax on wages, in a context where the correct application of the collective labor agreement (CLA) has become, as reiterated by the OCST, an absolute priority. It is not just about defining new parameters but ensuring that what is agreed is fully respected by companies. The union has clarified its stance for the next six years: uncompromising and consistent monitoring of working conditions, as expressed by the base, because, as stated, it is of no use to write a good contract if it is not applied in practice. The focus therefore shifts from the negotiation plane to the field control, ensuring that every worker sees their agreed rights recognized without exceptions or discretionary interpretations by employers, in a labor market that requires ever greater transparency and respect for the rules in force in Canton Ticino.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Procedures and protection of rights
In light of the contractual changes defined in May 2026, the main challenge for construction workers lies in the application of vigilance. The signing of a six-year contract requires careful management of site dynamics. For those working as cross-border workers, it is advisable to periodically verify that the new amounts related to site allowances and salary adjustments for the cost of living are correctly reported on the pay slip. In case of doubts about the correct application of the new contractual rules, the correct procedure involves direct discussion with the competent trade union bodies, such as the OCST, which actively participated in the definition of the agreement. It is essential to maintain precise documentation of working hours, especially in light of the new regulation on travel time, which must be counted from the first minute, without the application of the thirty-year exemption. This documentation is essential if a verification of compliance between what is agreed in the CBA and what is actually paid by the company is necessary. Respect for the collective agreement is a right that must be claimed consistently. The position taken by the union is clear: intransigence will be the guiding line for the next few years, in order to ensure that the generational turnover of the construction sector does not occur to the detriment of the quality and safety of work, but through an overall improvement of the image of the profession. Regarding the fiscal and contributory management of one's income, including aspects related to withholding tax or AVS/LPP social security, it is always advisable to consult simulation tools to fully understand the impact of salary changes on net income. It is possible to deepen one's salary situation using the [tax calculator](nav:calculator) to obtain a clear projection of the net pay slip following the increases and new allowances. Staying informed and proactive in monitoring one's rights represents the best tool available to operate safely in the Ticino labor market, ensuring that every contractual improvement effectively translates into a concrete benefit for one's personal and family budget.

## Key facts - **What**: Awareness campaign on basic skills (reading, writing, calculating, using the computer) - When: Start of September 2026, events 5-10 September - Where: Bellinzona, Biasca, Chiasso, Locarno, Lugano, Monte Carasso - Who: UFCI (Professional Training Division), Reading and Writing Association of Italian Switzerland, Conference of Italian Switzerland - Inspiration: National campaign 'Simply better!' - Slogan: 'Reading makes your life easier', 'Writing makes you independent', 'Calculating saves you money', 'Using the computer can help you'
At the beginning of September, the Continuing Education and Innovation Office (UFCI) of the Cantonal Professional Training Division will launch an awareness campaign on basic skills. The initiative, coordinated with the Reading and Writing Association of Italian Switzerland and the Conference of Italian Switzerland for Adult Continuing Education, aims to highlight the importance of four fundamental pillars: reading, writing, calculating, and using the computer.
The campaign will be developed through large stickers placed in the main public spaces of Bellinzona, Biasca, Chiasso, Locarno, and Lugano. The four slogans of the initiative — 'Reading makes your life easier', 'Writing makes you independent', 'Calculating saves you money', and 'Using the computer can help you' — take up the message of the national campaign 'Simply better!', adapting it to the Ticinese context.
### Why basic skills remain critical
According to the DECS, basic skills are essential for dealing with daily activities that every Ticino resident encounters regularly: filling out online forms, managing the family budget, purchasing public transport tickets. However, these skills are not definitive: they can weaken over time and require constant updating, especially in a context marked by increasing digitization.
For those living in Ticino, the ability to read written instructions, write and communicate, do calculations, and navigate computer platforms is a critical element in modern life. From filling out an online administrative form to managing personal accounts, from email communications to digital purchases, the basic skills of the UFCI campaign are skills directly applied every day. These are not elementary notions but strategic skills to maintain autonomy and dignity in the contemporary context. ## The September Program: Five Days of Awareness
The campaign calendar is dense and articulated. **On September 5 **, at the Greenday in Bellinzona, you can take part in an interactive experience in the Millestrade van, set up as an escape room. Here visitors can try their hand at puzzles, applying logical reasoning and reading skills in a practical way.
September 8 marks International Literacy Day. On this occasion, the campaign will be present from 7 am at the stations of Bellinzona and Lugano, making the initiative accessible to those who pass through these main railway junctions.
### ### Docufilm and special evening: the cultural programme
The three films will be screened at different dates and places: 5 September in Bellinzona, 7 September in Locarno and 9 September in Chiasso. This geographical distribution allows those who reside in different areas of Ticino — from Sopraceneri to Sottoceneri, up to the border areas — to access the content without the need for long journeys.
Among the main events is the evening "The stories never leave you", scheduled for 10 September at 20:00 at the Ancient Convent of the Augustinian Sisters of Monte Carasso. The event is dedicated to the writer Andrea Vitali, who will be present. The evening highlights the role of reading as a core competence of the UFCI campaign.

If you live in Ticino and are interested in discovering the details of this campaign, the process is simple and free.
Step 1: Align your calendar around the three docufilms. Want to participate in Bellinzona? On September 5. Prefer Locarno (Sopraceneri)? On September 7. Are you closer to Chiasso (Italian border)? On September 9. Each screening is a concrete introduction to the theme of continuous training.
Step 2: Participate in the Greenday in Bellinzona (September 5). If you are in Bellinzona on September 5 — perhaps commuting or taking a break from your work routine — stop by the Greenday and take on the Millestrade escape room challenge. It's a fun way to experience firsthand how basic skills (logic, reading, quick calculation) are applied in real and immediate contexts.
Step 3: Visit a main station on September 8. From 7 in the morning, get in touch with the campaign team at the Bellinzona or Lugano station. It's an ideal moment if you are in transit — perfect for those who start early towards their daily activities.
### The special evening and the continuation of training
Step 4: Register for the special evening in Monte Carasso (September 10, 8 PM). For those who intend to deepen the theme of reading and storytelling — and meet the writer Andrea Vitali — the evening "Stories Never Let You Go" at the Antico Convento delle Agostiniane is a moment of reflection and community.
These five days represent the public launch of the campaign, but continuous training does not stop in September. Many Ticino organizations — schools, public entities, cultural associations — offer structured courses on basic skills. For those who are busy and want to develop their professional profile — perhaps to advance in their career, move to a role with greater digital responsibilities, or prepare for a sector transition — it is crucial to identify recognized training programs. The Canton Ticino and its partners have dedicated resources.
If you work in Ticino and are looking for professional development opportunities, or want to check how updated skills can increase your employment prospects in the local market, [consult the available job opportunities](nav:jobs) in the territory. Many Ticino employers explicitly seek candidates with strong digital skills and solid basic skills — and the UFCI campaign is a public signal that this need is recognized at the institutional level.

## In brief - Permit G for cross-border commuters living in Italy and working in Switzerland - New Cross-Border Agreement effective from 1 January 2024: refunds up to €7,500 for old cross-border commuters - Withholding tax deducted in Switzerland, foreign tax credit in Italy (form CE of the 730) - AVS, LPP, and LAMal managed entirely in Switzerland for cross-border commuters
## Key facts - **Who**: Cross-border commuters with Permit G living in Albavilla (Como, Italy) and working in Canton Ticino - What: Swiss tax and social security regime, with AVS/LPP/LAMal rights - When: New Agreement in force from 1 January 2024 - Where: Albavilla (Como) ↔ Ticino, Brogeda, Chiasso, Gaggiolo border crossings - Amount: Exemption €10,000 (new cross-border commuters) or €7,500 (old cross-border commuters, transitional regime 2024–2033)
In Albavilla, a town near Como, hundreds of cross-border commuters have chosen to live in Italy while continuing to work in Ticino. This trend reflects a balanced strategy: living where the cost of living is lower but earning in Swiss francs. To work in Switzerland while residing in Italy, the Permit G (cross-border commuter) is essential, allowing daily entries and exits from the Ticino territory.
### The tax and social security regime of the cross-border commuter
The foundation of the tax situation for those living in Albavilla and working in Ticino is a special regime. Unlike an Italian employee, the cross-border commuter is subject to Swiss withholding tax, calculated directly on the salary by the Ticino employer and paid to the cantonal administration. This deduction occurs ONLY in Switzerland: Italy does not apply parallel taxation on cross-border commuter income, as the Italo-Swiss Convention (signed on 9 December 1976) and the New Cross-Border Agreement provide for foreign tax credit to avoid double taxation.
Social security contributions are managed entirely by the Swiss system. The AVS (old-age and survivors' insurance) is deducted at 5.3% from the employee, supplemented by the employer's contribution. The LPP (occupational pension, second pillar) varies from 7 to 18% depending on the age bracket, with access starting from 25 years. The cross-border commuter also pays contributions for AD/AC (unemployment/integration insurance) at 1.1% and for accident insurance LAINF (0.7–1.5%). Overall, these costs are lower than what an Italian resident would pay to the INPS.
Health insurance (LAMal) is mandatory in Switzerland for those who work there. The cross-border commuter in Albavilla has the option to choose: they can opt for a Swiss LAMal (through the employer or individually) or maintain Italian coverage. The Swiss LAMal is generally preferred by cross-border commuters, with deductibles ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 depending on the selected plan.
### The new 2024 agreement and automatic refunds
Starting from 1 January 2024, the New Cross-Border Agreement introduces an automatic refund mechanism for those who fall within certain income thresholds. Cross-border commuters who had already started their activity before 17 July 2023 ('old cross-border commuters') benefit from an annual exemption of €7,500, with a transitional regime until 2033. New cross-border commuters (hired after 17 July 2023) have an exemption of €10,000. If the annual income does not exceed these limits, there is automatically no risk of double taxation, and the Ticino administration calculates the refunds automatically, without the need for an explicit request. Those who exceed the exemption must still verify if they are entitled to the Italian tax credit by completing form CE of the 730 model. ### Daily commuting and distance from border crossings
Albavilla is approximately 30–40 kilometers from the main Ticino border crossings (Brogeda, Chiasso, Gaggiolo). This proximity to the border is one of the factors that attracts cross-border workers to municipalities like Albavilla: by reducing travel times, fuel costs, vehicle maintenance, and overall wear and tear are minimized. A cross-border worker who works in Mendrisio or Chiasso will face significantly shorter commuting times compared to someone living in Como or in the more inland areas of the Como province.
The road connection is ensured by the A2 and A9 highways (in Swiss territory) and the Lombardy links leading to the Brogeda (access to Ticino) and Gaggiolo (via Como) border crossings. During periods of heavy traffic or in case of union strikes in Switzerland, transit times at the border crossings can increase considerably: it is advisable to check road conditions before each crossing and plan adequate time margins on critical days.
### Cost of living: Albavilla vs. Canton Ticino
The cost of living in Lombardy, especially in the province of Como, is generally lower than in the Canton Ticino. Rent, food expenses, household utilities, public transportation: each budget item contributes to a significant difference. For a cross-border worker, this dynamic translates into a tangible economic advantage: receiving a salary in Swiss francs (higher than comparable Italian salaries) and paying living and housing expenses in Italian euros generates a substantial net gain. Albavilla, located a short distance from Como and immersed in the quiet residential areas of the Como belt, offers a variety of properties at significantly lower prices compared to the Ticino market.
Use the [nav:cost-of-living] tool on the site to compare monthly costs between Albavilla and your workplace in Ticino (Mendrisio, Lugano, Bellinzona, Locarno), so you can accurately assess the potential savings in your case.
### AVS and complementary pension: rights and monitoring
A cross-border worker residing in Albavilla accumulates all pension rights in the Swiss system (AVS and LPP), not in the Italian system (INPS). This means that the future pension will be calculated entirely on a Swiss basis: AVS pension rates are generally lower than those of the Italian INPS, but the contribution is proportional and fair compared to salaries. Important: those who accumulate less than 43 years of contributions do not qualify for a full AVS pension. It is advisable to periodically monitor the AVS registers (by accessing your online insurance account) to verify that all years of work have been correctly recorded.
The **LPP** (Swiss company pension fund, second pillar) is linked to the employment contract with the Ticino employer. In case of a change of company or loss of employment, the LPP balance can be transferred to a freely chosen institution (individual pension policy) or to an open pension fund. The Swiss system offers greater flexibility compared to the Italian INPS: it allows for early withdrawals for the purchase of the main residence (art. 19c, LPP), a possibility appreciated by cross-border workers.
### Tax declaration and management of double taxation
A cross-border worker in Albavilla pays withholding tax in Switzerland but remains obliged to file the annual Italian tax return (Model 730 or Redditi PF). In the CE section of the declaration, they enter the foreign tax credit for the Swiss tax already paid, formally avoiding double taxation. Thanks to the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement (in effect from January 1, 2024), if the annual income falls within the exemption (€7,500 for old cross-border workers, €10,000 for new ones), the Ticino administration automatically calculates the tax refund without explicit request. If the income exceeds the threshold, the refund is calculated proportionally. It is essential to keep the Swiss tax certificate provided by the employer (AVS account statement, withholding tax declaration) to support the Italian tax credit with the Revenue Agency.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Recruitment Procedure and Permit G: the administrative steps
The administrative path to become a Ticino border worker begins with the search for a job offer in Ticino. Once an employer has been found willing to hire you, it is the Ticino company that initiates the application procedure for the G Permit at the Swiss Secretariat of State for Migration (SEM). It is not necessary to submit any preliminary personal application: the employer formalises the application, attaching the employment contract and personal documentation (valid passport, criminal certificate, declaration of residence in Italy). Once the permit has been obtained, it is essential to register with the competent cantonal office in Ticino and communicate the change of situation to the Italian Revenue Agency.
### Preliminary checklist for transfer to Albavilla
Before you settle permanently in Albavilla, review these key points:
**1. Registered residence**: Transfer the residence from the municipality of origin to the municipality of Albavilla at the local registry office. Keep the transfer declaration and the residence certificate; these documents are essential for Italian taxation and for the recognition of border status.
2. Health insurance: Decide between a Swiss LAMal (through the employer or individually) and maintaining Italian coverage. Swiss LAMal is generally more advantageous

item.description: Moving to border Italy and working in Ticino: tax advantages, procedures allowed, costs of living and impact on paycheck.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Withholding tax deducted ONLY in Switzerland; tax credit in Italy via 730 - New cross-border agreement effective from January 1, 2024: €10,000 allowance for new cross-border workers - Permit G: access to Swiss employment with stable residence in border Italy - Mandatory AVS 5.3% for the employee; LAMal Swiss health insurance with CHF 300–2500 deductibles
## Key facts - **What**: Living in Solbiate con Cagno (Como) and working in Switzerland as a cross-border worker category G - When: New Cross-Border Agreement effective from January 1, 2024 - Where: Solbiate con Cagno (Italy, Como) and Canton Ticino (Switzerland), accessible via Brogeda and Gaggiolo crossings - Who: Italian cross-border workers (new from July 17, 2023) - Taxation: Withholding tax in Switzerland; €10,000 annual income allowance for new cross-border workers - AVS: Employee contribution 5.3%, with access to the Swiss public pension system - LAMal: Mandatory Swiss health insurance with the option for category G cross-border workers
Solbiate con Cagno is a municipality in the province of Como, a few kilometers from the Ticino border. In recent years, it has attracted Italian cross-border workers interested in working for companies, public entities, and institutions in Italian Switzerland. The choice to reside in border Italy while maintaining employment in Ticino responds to multiple factors: tax advantages derived from the New Cross-Border Agreement that came into effect on January 1, 2024, lower cost of living in Italy compared to Ticino, and geographical proximity to the main Ticino employment basins.
The New Cross-Border Agreement, signed on December 23, 2020, and ratified by Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023, revises the tax and contribution regime for those living in Italy and working in Switzerland. Cross-border workers are subject to withholding tax deducted ONLY by the Swiss employer. Italy avoids double taxation by recognizing this tax as a credit in the annual declaration (CE section of the 730 form). New cross-border workers (not resident in Italy before July 17, 2023) benefit from a €10,000 allowance on employment income. This tax advantage translates into a significant reduction in the tax burden in the first years of transfer.
In addition to taxation, those choosing Solbiate con Cagno must consider Swiss administrative and contribution constraints. Permit G (cross-border) allows working in Switzerland with stable residence in Italy. Swiss pension contributions are mandatory: AVS (Old Age and Disability Insurance) at 5.3% for the employee, plus AD/AC (unemployment and calamity) contributions at 1.1% up to CHF 148,200 annually, and LPP (complementary pension insurance) at 7–18% according to the age bracket (from the 25th year of life). Additionally, mandatory enrollment in LAMal (Swiss health insurance) averages CHF 2000–3500 annually, with adult deductibles from CHF 300 to 2500.
For those residing in Solbiate con Cagno, the Ticino employment basin remains accessible through the Brogeda and Gaggiolo crossings. The choice to move to Italy while maintaining employment in Ticino represents a balance between economic benefits (Swiss paycheck, access to robust pension systems like AVS and LPP, Italian tax allowance €10,000) and hidden costs (AVS/LAMal contributions, bank fees for CHF/EUR exchange, daily commuting). ### Economic analysis: is it worth living in Solbiate and working in Ticino?
The economic convenience depends on a close comparison between the Italian cost of living, the Swiss paycheck, and the combined tax pressure Switzerland-Italy. In general, housing costs (rent, real estate purchase) in the province of Como are lower than Ticino prices. A commuter with a gross annual income of CHF 70,000 (approximately €66,000 equivalent) will pay withholding tax according to the Ticino cantonal rates, with additional tax credit recognized in Italy through the 730 declaration. The €10,000 exemption for new commuters reduces the Italian taxable income, creating a favorable tax effect in the first years of transfer.
However, hidden costs erode the gross advantage. The Swiss LAMal health insurance costs an average of CHF 2000–3500 annually for an adult, depending on the chosen deductible. To this, add the AVS contributions (5.3% employee) and LPP (7–18% depending on age), deducted directly from the paycheck. On the Italian side, commuters remain enrolled in INPS for the redemption of periods not covered by AVS and maintain declaration obligations with the Agenzia delle Entrate. Additional costs: bank fees for dual-currency CHF-EUR management, Swiss highway vignette (CHF 40 annually), parking at border crossings.
### Advantages for the commuter
- **Access to robust pension systems**: AVS (public old-age pension) and LPP (occupational second pillar) guarantee a high pension level, superior to the average Italian INPS - Lower cost of living: housing and services in the Como area cost less than in Ticino; a single residence reduces duplications - Job stability: the Ticino job market offers high salaries in CHF, with protection from Italian economic fluctuations - Tax exemption: new commuters benefit from an annual €10,000 deduction from Italian income in the first years
### Disadvantages and risks
- Daily commuting: trips from Solbiate to Ticino generate stress, vehicle wear, time cost, personal pollution - Double tax administration: although simplified by the 2024 agreement, it requires diligence in the annual 730 declaration - CHF/EUR exchange rate volatility: money transfers from Ticino to Como are subject to currency fluctuations - G permit constraints: changing employer requires permit renewal; job loss can jeopardize residence in Italy
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-step procedure: how to move to Solbiate and become a cross-border worker
Phase 1: Obtaining Permit G (cross-border work) The first step is to obtain Permit G from the Swiss authorities (Migration Section of the Canton Ticino, or SEM — State Secretariat for Migration). Required documents: valid passport or identity document, signed employment contract with a registered Swiss employer, residence certificate from the Municipality of Solbiate with Cagno, complete SEM application form. Permit G is tied to the employment relationship: changing employers requires renewal.
Phase 2: Tax registration with the Federal Tax Administration (FTA) The Swiss employer will open the tax management with the FTA. The cross-border worker must communicate the Italian tax code and Permit G number. The FTA collects the withholding tax according to the cantonal rate of Ticino applied to the gross monthly income, deducted directly from the paycheck.
Phase 3: Enrollment in LAMal within 3 months The cross-border worker must sign a health insurance contract with a Swiss insurance company (Helsana, Concordia, CSS, etc.). Choose a deductible (CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, or 2500 annually). Essential services covered at 100% (hospital, medications, basic medical visits).
Phase 4: Communication to the Italian Revenue Agency Communicate the Italian residence to the Revenue Agency (Income section) and report employment in Switzerland with the Permit G number. In the annual model 730, section CE (foreign tax credit), report the withholding tax paid in Switzerland and apply a €10,000 exemption on the gross income (if a new cross-border worker).
Phase 5: Opening a dual-currency bank account It is advisable to open an account with a bank that operates in CHF-EUR to facilitate transfers from the employer and minimize exchange fees. Banks in Ticino and Italian institutions with branches in Como offer this solution.
### Pre-move checklist
- ✓ Signed employment contract with a Swiss employer - ✓ Valid identity document + passport - ✓ Residence certificate from the Municipality of Solbiate with Cagno - ✓ Complete SEM application form for Permit G request - ✓ Dual-currency CHF-EUR bank account - ✓ Scanned copy of Permit G once obtained - ✓ LAMal subscription within 3 months from the start of employment - ✓ Communication to the Revenue Agency before the first 730 declaration
Before formalizing the move, use the [pay slip calculator](nav:payslip) to estimate the net monthly income considering AVS (5.3%), LAMal (CHF 200–300 monthly), cantonal rates of Ticino, and Italian tax credit. This will allow you to verify the real economic convenience and plan your personal budget.
